title: A proof of the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture on entropy maximization for cube projections
summary: We complete the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture: among the one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube, differential entropy is maximized precisely in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. Pang proved the conjecture in every dimension at least $150$. We prove the remaining dimensions using polynomial entropy bounds in dimensions three through six and exact certificates for derivatives of the logarithm of the diagonal projection density. The proof uses integer arithmetic and certified one-dimensional integration. We also derive quantitative stability estimates and determine the optimal asymptotic coefficient of a linear stability bound. The source code and the outputs of all finite verifications accompany the paper.

title: Surrogate Symbols in Wireless Communications
summary: Co-channel interference (CCI), caused by the inevitable aggressive channel reuse in dense deployments, remains a critical bottleneck for current and future wireless communication systems. In this paper, we address this bottleneck in an N-co-channel wireless communications network of single-antenna transmitters and receivers. The limiting case of this problem leads to a novel "thought experiment": If each receiver's own desired channel link is simultaneously completely blocked, can a Maximum Likelihood Detection at each receiver still recover its transmitted symbol? In the traditional way of thinking, the answer is no: The receiver obtains nothing but co-channel interference (CCI) plus thermal noise, and a receiver-side phase rotation cannot help, since there is no desired signal to align. Given only the channel matrix H -- and no knowledge of the transmitted symbols -- can the transmitters' phases be chosen so that the received signal becomes "almost" the desired symbol at every receiver? We show that the answer is yes. We first develop the underlying framework for the general case (nonzero own-channel link case), turning classical co-channel systems into a novel discrete phase-optimization problem, "Game of Phases: Surrogate Symbol Optimization", and present two algorithms, "Minimum Phased-Interference Power algorithm (MiPIP)" and "Maximum Phased-Interference Support (MaPRIS)". We then show that the MaPRIS resolves the thought experiment: it converts hostile CCI into an "almost" desired symbol even when the own desired channel link is zero, yielding the counter-intuitive result that higher CCI variance yields higher SINR. Extensive simulation results confirm the findings. The gain promised by the proposed algorithms comes on top of any other CCI reduction techniques as our framework here is based on a bottom-line baseband model.

title: Joint Channel Estimation, Data Detection, and Phase Noise Tracking in Massive MIMO Systems
summary: Communication over multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is degraded by phase noise (PN) arising from imperfect local oscillators, with PN becoming more severe at higher carrier frequencies. Existing methods either rely on linearized Kalman-filter approaches or apply variational Bayes (VB) only to individual stages, such as data detection under a static phase prior, or channel estimation alone, leaving no unified framework that tracks an evolving PN process consistently across pilot and data transmission. This paper develops such a framework for uplink massive MIMO. Specifically, we first propose VB-Tracking, which employs von Mises priors and coordinate-ascent VB inference to jointly estimate the channel and track the transmit and receive PN trajectories during the pilot phase without linearization. We then propose VB-Detecting for joint data detection and phase tracking by absorbing the transmit PN into a composite transmit variable. Using a sequentially propagated von Mises predictive prior, the composite variable admits an exact closed-form posterior. Finally, we propose VB-Refining, which periodically re-estimates the channel during data transmission using the soft posterior moments of reliably detected transmit symbols as virtual pilots. We show that VB-Detecting scales linearly in the number of users, receive antennas, constellation size, and iterations. Simulations against EKF-EP, EKF-ZF, and JED baselines show that VB-Tracking, VB-Detecting, and VB-Refining together achieve lower channel NMSE and symbol error rate, with the performance gap widening at high SNR and under severe PN.

title: Non-Uniform Array Configuration and Antenna Deactivation for Energy-Efficient Sensing
summary: This paper proposes a non-uniform array design framework for energy-efficient multi-target sensing by jointly optimizing the antenna configuration and the transmit covariance matrix (TCM). To begin with, a limited number of antennas are selected from a set of antenna locations to maximize the minimum mainlobe-to-peak-sidelobe-level ratio (MMPSR) over a sensing region. Next, the antenna configuration is optimized using a simulated annealing (SA)-based search, while a TCM optimization problem is formulated using Charnes-Cooper transformation and solved as a convex semidefinite program for each fixed configuration. Subsequently, an adaptive antenna deactivation strategy is developed to determine the maximum number of antennas that can be switched off while satisfying an MMPSR requirement. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed non-uniform array design outperforms fixed uniform and non-uniform array benchmarks and requires fewer active antennas to achieve a required sensing performance, thereby supporting energy-efficient sensing.

title: New constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for quasi-block monotone Ferrers diagrams
summary: Constant dimension subspace codes (CDCs) have become an important object in coding theory due to their applications in random network coding. The paper is devoted to constructing optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block Ferrers diagrams, which play a crucial role in the multilevel construction of CDCs. Let \(\mathbb{F}_q\) be the finite field with \(q\) elements of characteristic \(p\), \(P\) be a power of \(p\), and \(e\) be a positive integer. Let \(L=\mathbb F_{q^{eP}}\) and \(\sigma\) be the Frobenius \(\mathbb F_q\)-automorphism of \(L\), set \(N=\sigma^e-\mathrm{id}\). Based on the multiplicative property of the kernel filtration of the nilpotent map \(N\), we construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block monotone diagrams. Specifically, considering \(n \times l\) Ferrers diagrams, we prove that optimal codes always exist for block monotone diagrams when \(n = eP\). Furthermore, by employing puncturing on columns, we prove that optimal codes also always exist for block strictly monotone diagrams, removing the restriction \(n = eP\). Consequently, optimal codes always exist for block upper triangular diagrams, specifically for maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD)-constructible block diagram pairs, which generalizes the corresponding results in \cite{neri2024,calderini2026}, in which the rank distance or the characteristic is restricted. Furthermore, by employing both puncturing and shortening on columns, we prove that optimal codes always exist for quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams, thereby generalizing the corresponding results in \cite{pratihar2023, zhang2019}. The optimal codes constructed in this paper will potentially be beneficial to the further construction of CDCs.

title: Joint RF-VLP Position and Velocity Tracking: Bayesian Estimation and Performance Analysis
summary: Visible light positioning (VLP) provides accurate indoor positioning through optical received signal strength (RSS) measurements, while radio-frequency (RF) delay and Doppler measurements offer complementary range and velocity information. Motivated by this complementarity, we investigate joint RF--VLP position and velocity tracking, addressing both recursive state estimation and its fundamental performance characteristics. We formulate a Bayesian maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem that combines optical RSS, RF delay and Doppler measurements, and motion prediction, and develop a Gauss--Newton-based algorithm for recursive tracking. To characterize the estimation limits and the benefits of RF--VLP integration, we derive the Bayesian information matrix and the corresponding Bayesian Cramér--Rao lower bound (BCRLB). We further introduce a state-conditioned information matrix (SCIM), whose inverse coincides with the MAP estimator's mean-squared error matrix under a first-order observation model, enabling tractable analysis of RF-induced information gains. The analysis quantifies the distinct contributions of RF delay and Doppler measurements and reveals different asymptotic estimation-error behaviors with respect to RF and VLP signal-to-noise ratios. Numerical results demonstrate improved position and velocity tracking over the considered baselines, with substantial velocity gains from RF sensing. The results also validate the theoretical asymptotic predictions and show that the inverse of the SCIM closely captures the estimator's error trends.

title: HDR-DTCP: High-Dynamic-Range Differential Tissue-Coupled Wireless Powering for Tunable Biphasic Stimulation in Injectable Implants
summary: Next-generation implantable neurostimulators require efficient wireless power delivery in smaller, less invasive form factors, yet variations in tissue coupling, implantation conditions, and stimulation loads can alter received power (or requirements) and degrade energy-harvesting performance. This work presents high-dynamic-range (HDR) differential tissue-coupled powering (DTCP), termed HDR-DTCP, a body-coupled architecture in which noninvasive differential electrodes establish an AC electric field in tissue and a thread-like implant extracts power from the longitudinal potential gradient for on-chip harvesting and stimulation. Distributed coupling along the implant length, rather than receiver cross-section, enables minimally invasive injectable geometries, with harvested power scaling with implant length. A 65-nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) prototype integrates a reconfigurable four-stage energy harvester with automatic stage selection and a tunable constant-current biphasic stimulator, achieving 63.5\% peak power-conversion efficiency (PCE) at $-16.3$ dBm and $>50\%$ PCE over a 9-dB input-power range. Preliminary in-vivo validation of DTCP was done with a second application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) on an injectable flexible substrate, capable of being delivered through a 14-gauge needle adjacent to the sciatic nerve of Sprague-Dawley rats (n=4). External copper-pad DTCP powering evoked repeatable hind-limb twitches and electromyography (EMG) response; ultrasound confirmed sub-millimeter nerve proximity, video-based paw-tip tracking captured the response, and 8-day post-implant dissection verified placement along the sciatic-nerve trajectory. Overall, this work provides an integrated wireless powering, energy-harvesting, and stimulation platform toward fully battery-free injectable neuromodulation implants.

title: Joint Movable Antenna Positioning and Precoding for ISAC via a Two-Timescale Model-Based GNN
summary: Movable antennas (MAs) allow an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) base station (BS) to reshape multiuser channels and angular sensitivity. For monostatic multiuser communication and multi-target elevation and azimuth estimation, we minimize the expected target-averaged angular Bayesian Cramér-Rao bound (BCRB) subject to per-user block-level and long-term rate requirements. To avoid repeated online optimization, we propose a two-timescale model-based graph neural network (TT-MBGNN) over antennas, users, and targets. The slow policy selects positions from long-term statistics to reduce movement overhead, while the fast policy learns complex corrections to a regularized zero-forcing (RZF) reference using post-movement channels and target-angle priors. We jointly train both policies through a differentiable model of rates and BCRB, without optimization-generated labels. Across tested rate requirements, the network yields lower sensing bounds than variants using a fixed array, RZF, or both, with any-user fast-rate violations in 0.31-2.63% of test blocks. Frozen policies provide competitive sensing bounds for unseen user and target counts, and ten fine-tuning epochs improve communication reliability at higher user counts. Across tested network sizes, our framework achieves up to 3 dB lower BCRB than an idealized alternating-optimization benchmark that uses known target reflection coefficients. The network computes precoders approximately 50-fold faster in matched batch-one tests.

title: What Makes Good Datasets for Intelligent Multi-Modal Sensing-Communication Integration?
summary: Intelligent multi-modal sensing-communication integration, namely Synesthesia of Machines (SoM), represents an AI-native paradigm for enabling embodied intelligence and future wireless networks. Multi-modal sensing and communication foundation models developed for SoM learn cross-modal associations and generalizable environmental representations through large-scale pretraining, making the quality of pretraining datasets critical. However, existing methods lack unified evaluation of heterogeneous multi-modal data and thus struggle to meet the requirements for multi-modal pretraining dataset construction and selection. To bridge this gap, we introduce a comprehensive data evaluation framework for intelligent multi-modal sensing-communication integration. Specifically, we establish two complementary heterogeneous multi-modal data evaluation dimensions, including intrinsic data quality and validity, and model-based data utility. Furthermore, we present case studies to validate the effectiveness of the two evaluation dimensions. We also extend our analysis to investigate the impact of data quality on pretraining scaling laws and explore the value of integrating measurement and simulation data. Finally, we outline promising directions for future research on data evaluation.

title: Entropy-Based and Quadratic Conditional Innovation Metrics for Informed Dynamic Scheduling of Belief-Propagation Decoding for LDPC Codes
summary: We propose two enhanced conditional innovation (CI) metrics for informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) in belief-propagation (BP) decoding of LDPC codes. The CI-based residual BP (CIRBP) algorithm uses the CI metric to guide the selection of the variable node (VN) to be updated and has been shown to outperform several existing IDS-based BP decoders, especially at the early decoding stage. However, the original CI metric uses only the absolute difference between the current and precomputed posterior probabilities and does not separately account for the reliability associated with each probability. By reformulating the CI metric relative to the decision boundary, we separate each posterior probability into its decision side and a linear-distance term reflecting reliability. Replacing the latter with the binary entropy complement yields the proposed entropy-based CI (E-CI) metric. Moreover, the proposed quadratic CI (Q-CI) metric is derived from the leading quadratic term in the local expansion of the entropy complement, avoiding the logarithmic operations required for direct E-CI evaluation. We apply both proposed metrics to the CIRBP decoder and its node-wise variant. Numerical results show that the proposed metrics generally provide lower frame error rates than the original CI metric, with their relative advantages depending on the code and decoding procedure.

title: Sensing with OFDM Signals: How Do the Constellations Affect the Sensing Accuracy?
summary: This paper investigates how communication constellations affect joint range-velocity estimation with data-bearing orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. To this end, starting from the continuous-time sensing process, we derive a discrete observation model and specify its validity conditions. For multiple targets with unknown delays, Doppler shifts, and complex gains, the complete Fisher information matrix (FIM) admits a structural factorization separating deterministic channel derivatives from random symbol-energy weights. This structure yields a Jensen-type lower bound on the average conditional Cramer-Rao bound (CRB), which is attained exactly by constant-modulus constellations. Single-target closed-form expressions further reveal the dependence of the bounds on the transmitted energy distribution and physical OFDM parameters. We also formulate two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (FFT), concentrated maximum-likelihood (ML), and sliding-subarray multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing under the derived observation model. Numerical results support the theoretical optimality of constant-modulus constellations but also show that the CRB gap between phase-shift keying (PSK) and quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) becomes negligible when the numbers of subcarriers and OFDM symbols are considerably large. The performance of ML estimation closely approaches the derived bounds, which confirms the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis. FFT processing exhibits grid-induced error floors. In the considered scenarios, MUSIC provides lower estimation errors than FFT and exhibits a more pronounced constellation dependence.

title: Fundamental Limits of Statistical Watermarking for LLMs with Fixed and Optimizable Common Randomness
summary: Watermarking has emerged as an important technique for distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text. However, most existing work is primarily empirical, relies on ad hoc watermarking designs, and lacks a fundamental understanding of the performance limits. In this paper, we propose a unified theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of large language models (LLMs), casting the problem as an independence test between generated text and common randomness and jointly designing the watermarking embedder and the detector. Our objective is to maximize detection power while controlling the worst-case false positive rate (FPR) and limiting distortion to text quality. A central focus of our framework is the design of the common randomness, which plays a critical role in both watermark embedding and detection. We characterize the fundamental limits of statistical watermarking under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. Our results show that optimizing the common randomness does not improve the fundamental limits: the best achievable performance is the same as that with fixed common randomness. Nevertheless, common randomness design remains highly important because it can substantially simplify detector design. In particular, with optimizable common randomness, a fixed, deterministic, and model-agnostic detector can achieve optimal performance. We further study a practical setting with fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector, and characterize its performance gap relative to the optimizable case, thereby demonstrating the practical value of optimizable common randomness.

title: Active-Element Configuration for Energy-Efficient Secure Near-Field ISAC With Hybrid RISs
summary: Hybrid active-passive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (HRISs) are promising for secure near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) through selective signal amplification and spherical-wave beam focusing. However, fixed active-element layouts limit flexibility in exploiting element-dependent near-field channels while balancing secrecy performance, sensing accuracy, and circuit power consumption. This paper develops a joint active-element configuration and transmission design for a large-aperture HRIS-assisted system, where sensing targets act as potential eavesdroppers. The design adapts both the number and spatial distribution of active elements by exploiting near-field phase and attenuation variations. We establish a bidirectional signal and power model with full-aperture reflection and active-subset amplification for downlink signals and uplink echoes. Based on the derived three-dimensional localization Cramér-Rao bound, we formulate a mixed-integer non-convex secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem under user-rate, localization, and power constraints. To solve this problem, we propose an alternating optimization framework combining successive convex approximation, a penalty convex-concave procedure, and full-aperture reweighted group-sparse selection. The selection method scores and ranks elements to generate binary candidate configurations without exhaustive search. After refining continuous HRIS variables for each candidate, we select the feasible configuration with the highest genuine SEE. Simulation results demonstrate higher SEE with lower base station transmit power than fixed-layout HRIS schemes and a fully passive RIS baseline.

title: DyTransRM: A Unified Simulation-to-Real Framework for Dynamic Radio Map Prediction
summary: Dynamic radio map (RM) prediction enables proactive wireless network control by forecasting future propagation conditions from historical observations. However, collecting temporally continuous and spatially dense real-world RMs is prohibitively expensive, while models trained on large-scale simulated data often suffer from limited transferability to real environments. To address this issue, we propose DyTransRM, a unified simulation-to-real framework for dynamic RM prediction under sparse real-world measurements. DyTransRM first introduces RadioCLIP to learn physics-semantic representations by aligning environmental evolution with the corresponding propagation evolution, thereby improving both prediction accuracy and cross-domain transferability. To further bridge the simulation-to-real gap, SparseUOT employs sparse-mask simulation refinement to mimic realistic measurement patterns and unbalanced optimal transport to selectively align compatible propagation representations across domains. Experiments on RadioMapMotion and real-world datasets demonstrate that RadioCLIP achieves an NMSE of 0.0018 and an RMSE of 0.012 in simulation-domain prediction. After sparse real-domain adaptation, DyTransRM achieves an NMSE of 0.023, RMSE of 0.079, and MAE of 0.064, outperforming representative adaptation baselines without requiring spatially complete real RMs. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DyTransRM for transferring simulation-learned dynamic propagation knowledge to practical sparse-measurement scenarios.

title: Over-the-Air Semantic Alignment via Dual Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
summary: Semantic communications enable task-oriented information exchange, but suffer from latent-space mismatch when transmitter and receiver employ heterogeneous machine learning models. Existing semantic alignment methods rely on digital processing, introducing computational and latency overhead. This paper proposes a dual stacked intelligent metasurfaces (dual-SIM) architecture that performs semantic alignment entirely in the wave domain. By jointly exploiting programmable metasurfaces at both ends of a link and the wireless channel, the proposed architecture realizes an end-to-end linear transformation between heterogeneous latent spaces. We show phase-only multilayer SIM can approximate both supervised linear aligners and zero-shot Parseval-frame equalizers. We investigate single-SIM, disjoint asymmetric and symmetric dual-SIM, and jointly optimized dual-SIM configurations, considering channel equalization and constructive channel exploitation. For joint design, we develop an alternating projected gradient algorithm with convergence guarantees to first-order stationary points. We further introduce a deep-unrolled network that unrolls gradient-based iterations to reduce computational cost of SIM reconfiguration under channel variations. Numerical results with heterogeneous vision transformer encoders show accurate semantic alignment from moderate to high signal-to-noise ratios. The joint and symmetric disjoint dual-SIM designs achieve the highest accuracy over compact channels, the joint design leads at shallow stack depths, and the advantage over single-SIM designs diminishes at equal depth.

title: On the boomerang spectrum of the APN power function $x^{q+2}$ over $\F_{q^2}$
summary: We study the boomerang spectrum of the almost perfect nonlinear power function $x^{q+2}$ over $\F_{q^2}$, where $q$ is an odd prime power with $q\equiv1\pmod6$. The connection of Pal and Stănică between boomerang entries and $(-1)$-differential entries reduces the problem to counting roots of a single equation. We determine the complete contribution from nonzero parameters in $\F_q$. For parameters outside $\F_q$, we obtain a quintic over $\F_q$ in terms of the parameter's trace and norm, with a separate formula when the trace is zero. We exclude the entry four when $q\equiv1\pmod{12}$ and characterize its occurrence when $q\equiv7\pmod{12}$ through a repeated-root parametrization and a residual cubic. We also evaluate the first nonsubfield moment and an aggregate quadratic-character sum, and prove a Weil bound for each nonzero trace. Explicit secant and residual-cubic formulas express the second, third, and fourth falling-factorial moments as finite sums. Once the size-four frequency is known, these moments recover all remaining frequencies through a nonsingular five-dimensional system. A closed-form evaluation of the nonsubfield distribution remains open.

title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect and Odd Perfect Sequences of Unbounded Length over the Unit Quaternions
summary: We give a recursive construction, with closed-form index functions, of perfect and odd perfect periodic autocorrelation sequences over the eight simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ in every length $2^n$. The sequences are built, as in the recursive perfect array construction of Blake, from \emph{twisted periodic extensions}: a short sequence continued with period $M$ up to a right factor $u\in\Qe$. Over roots of unity the twists cannot be regenerated by a one-dimensional recursion, consistently with Mow's conjecture; over $\Qe$ we show that no single sequence of length $M\not\equiv0\pmod 4$ carries a twist $\pm i,\pm j$ or $\pm k$ either, but that \emph{pairs} of sequences whose $i$- and $(-i)$-twisted autocorrelations are complementary do. These $i$-pairs behave exactly like Golay pairs: they double under interleaving with a right factor $j$ in place of a sign, every Golay pair of length $n$ gives an $i$-pair of length $2n$, and they exist in length $6$ where no Golay pair exists. An $i$-pair of length $M$ interleaves to an odd perfect sequence of length $4M$, and a perfect and an odd perfect sequence of length $M$ interleave to a perfect sequence of length $4M$ with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$. The $i$-pairs of length $2^t$ are $x^{(t)}_{r,a}=j^{w_t(r,a)}$, where $w_t(r,a)$ counts the changes in the bit string formed by $r$ and the binary digits of $a$, and the odd perfect sequence of length $2^{t+2}$ is $y^{(t)}_{2a+r}=j^{w_t(r,\,a\bmod 2^t)}\, i^{(1-2r)\lfloor a/2^t\rfloor}$. The construction also gives odd perfect sequences over $\Qe$ in every length $24\cdot2^s$ and perfect sequences in every length $6\cdot4^s$.

title: Exact Redundancy under Average and Almost-Sure Distortion Constraints
summary: We characterize the exact redundancy of lossy source coding under average and almost-sure distortion constraints. For general source and output alphabets, we establish the asymptotic redundancy coefficients under suitable regularity conditions. Under the average distortion constraint, the coefficient is half of the minimum probability that an output reveals information about the source, among all rate-distortion optimal channels. Under the almost-sure distortion constraint, the coefficient is either $1/2$ or $1$, depending on whether the $D$-tilted information is constant or not. Both converse results follow from a common change-of-measure inequality. Finally, we verify the required conditions under both distortion requirements always hold for finite alphabets.

title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
summary: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.

title: Hermitian Positive Definite Neural Networks for Matrix-CFAR Geometric Signal Detection in Nonhomogeneous Clutter
summary: Matrix information geometry (MIG) detectors exploit the Riemannian geometry of Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrices to achieve robust object detection in nonhomogeneous clutter. The matrix constant false alarm rate (matrix-CFAR) method is a representative MIG detector that relies on the geometric structures with respect to specific metrics. In most cases, computing representative HPD covariance matrices requires numerical methods, typically involving computationally intensive iterative optimization algorithms. Although explicit formulas are available for certain cases, such as the log-Euclidean (LE) mean, they are generally unavailable for many other matrix means and medians. To address this challenge, we propose integrating the Hermitian positive definite neural network (HPDNet) into the matrix-CFAR framework, replacing conventional numerical optimization procedures with a learned, geometry-preserving mapping that directly estimates representative HPD covariance matrices from data. In the simulations, the framework is evaluated for MIG detectors using both means and medians associated with the affine-invariant Riemannian metric, the LE metric, and the Bures--Wasserstein metric, on both simulated compound-Gaussian clutter and real IPIX sea clutter. In both cases, the HPDNet is trained solely on simulated data to assess its applicability to the study of real data. The results show a significant reduction of computational cost in testing, while maintaining detection performance and robustness.

title: Error-correcting codes without parity-check bits
summary: We are developing a new approach to the problem of error correction in communication channels, in which the input sequence is transformed in such a way that the interdependence of symbols increases significantly. Then, after the sequence is transmitted over the channel, this property is used for error correction, so that the residual error rate is significantly reduced. A natural example of its application is the transmission of binary sequences whose entropy (per symbol) is less than one, since in this case the length of the transmitted sequence remains constant during encoding and decoding. An algorithm has been developed to implement the maximum likelihood method, in which the encoding and decoding times are linear. This algorithm was used to experimentally investigate its effectiveness on popular channel models, and it was found that there are certain sets of parameters for which the proposed method is quite effective.

title: Wideband Hybrid Beamforming via Programmable Unitary Mixer--TTD RF Networks
summary: This paper proposes a wideband hybrid beamforming architecture whose analog front-end consists of fixed unitary mixers interlaced with programmable diagonal phase-shift/true-time-delay (TTD) layers. Under ideal passive-component assumptions, the analog beamformer is semi-unitary on every OFDM subcarrier, so the injected RF-chain power reaches the antenna ports without analog-network loss. We design the phase shifts and delays of the programmable diagonal phase-shift/TTD layers for OFDM sum-rate maximization. Numerical results show that increasing mixer--TTD depth improves the sum rate under ideal component assumptions and a common injected RF-power budget. With component losses included, a shallow design retains an advantage over the evaluated hybrid baselines at low-to-moderate powers, motivating deeper implementations with low accumulated loss.

title: Sparse Rotatable Arrays (SRAs) for Cell-Free MIMO: Network-Wide Design of Antenna Activation and Panel Orientation
summary: This paper investigates a sparse rotatable array (SRA)-enabled cell-free multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. Under a network-wide antenna activation budget, distributed access points (APs) select active antenna elements from their installed arrays and adjust panel orientations, enabling joint control of sparse array apertures and antenna directivity. To avoid frequent hardware reconfiguration in response to instantaneous channel variations, we formulate a two-timescale stochastic optimization problem to maximize the expected minimum-user rate. Long-term antenna activation and panel orientations are optimized based on user spatial distributions and statistical channel state information (CSI), while short-term precoders adapt to instantaneous CSI. Under line-of-sight (LoS) propagation, we derive the optimal single-user antenna allocation, characterize the two-user max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and establish conditions for discrete activation and panel rotation to attain the continuous-position benchmark, and obtain a closed-form multi-AP zero-forcing (ZF) allocation benchmark under a continuous antenna-count relaxation. For the general mixed-integer nonconvex stochastic problem, we develop an alternating algorithm based on sample-average approximation (SAA), integrating uplink-downlink (UL-DL) duality for short-term precoding, weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) surrogates for panel-orientation optimization, and multi-start greedy search for antenna activation. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed design outperforms the fixed-array benchmark, improves all-user service reliability with fewer active antennas, and adapts effectively to nonuniform user spatial distributions.

title: The ordered sum-rank metric and linearized multiplicity codes: NRT meets sum-rank
summary: In this work, we introduce linearized multiplicity codes, which are a common generalization of linearized Reed--Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes. We also introduce the ordered sum-rank metric, which is a common generalization of the sum-rank metric and the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric (or ordered Hamming metric). We provide a Singleton bound for the ordered sum-rank metric and show that linearized multiplicity codes attain it. That is, they are maximum ordered sum-rank distance (MOSRD) codes. We introduce the support lattice for the ordered sum-rank metric and study duality, support distributions and weight distributions of MOSRD codes. We also show that MOSRD codes are ordered MDS, dually quasi MSRD and, under some divisibility conditions, MSRD (and thus MDS). For linear MOSRD codes, we give lower bounds on the field extension degree by the number of matrix columns, and upper bounds on the block length by the base field size. We conclude by showing that linearized multiplicity codes attain such bounds exactly in almost all cases, and the same growth order in all cases.

title: SWAN-Rx: Efficient and Bandwidth-Scalable Neural Reception for MIMO-OFDM
summary: We present a Scalable Windowed Axial-attention Neural Receiver (SWAN-Rx) for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. The receiver improves reception accuracy and reduces forward-pass computation while supporting frozen-weight reuse across bandwidth allocations and channel conditions. It combines a common resource-element representation of received observations and pilot context with alternating time-axis and local frequency-axis attention. Shared parameters and relative positional information permit soft detection across allocation lengths without inference-time parameter updates. At fixed subcarrier spacing, model configuration, and symbol count, bounded frequency neighborhoods give linear growth of forward-pass computation with bandwidth. Evaluations compatible with the 5G New Radio physical layer reuse weights trained on four physical resource blocks (PRBs) at up to 273 PRBs and on unseen channels. At the training bandwidth, SWAN-Rx achieves lower pre- and post-decoding bit error rates than the implemented three-step neural receiver (NRX) and DeepRx-MIMO baselines, with 16.9% and 39.7% fewer parameters and 56.3% and 35.7% fewer forward-pass operations, respectively. The same weights achieve lower pre-decoding error rates than these baselines throughout the evaluated bandwidth-extrapolation and 16-PRB channel-transfer tests, with an estimated 0.4-0.9 dB signal-to-noise ratio reduction relative to NRX at a pre-decoding error rate of $10^{-2}$ in the 16-PRB tests.

title: Density-First Design of Anti-Jamming Sparse Spreading Codes for NB-IoT
summary: As narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) systems continue to be deployed in increasingly heterogeneous and demanding wireless environments, including those characterized by interference, high mobility, and potentially hostile conditions, enhancing the resilience of the physical-layer waveform has become an important and timely design consideration. Motivated by this need, the present paper introduces a density-first framework for the design of anti-jamming sparse spreading codes in NB-IoT systems. Building on this framework, we propose a generalized method for constructing sparse codes that decouples column density from the conventional Alamouti-paired structure, thereby enabling both disjoint-support and deterministic code designs. In addition, we develop a generative machine-learning approach based on a variational autoencoder for synthesizing jamming-robust sparse spreading codes. To evaluate the performance of sparse spreading under conditions of additive white Gaussian noise, fading, and pulse jamming, we present a bit-error-rate (BER) analysis framework. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations, conducted across a wide range of density, channel, and jamming conditions, show that the performance of sparse spreading codes is determined primarily by column density rather than by optimization of code coefficients. In particular, highly sparse codes with disjoint support offer the greatest robustness to jamming while avoiding the unfavorable intermediate-density regime. Relative to the prior-art Alamouti-paired low-density spreading code, the recommended uniform-density design reduces pulse-jamming BER by roughly 5 times; a deterministic Lempel-Costas construction attains the empirical optimum in closed form, while the variational-autoencoder generator yields a further 45% improvement over the best algebraic design.

title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Lookup Table Demappers for Amplitude Phase-Shift Keying over Nonlinear Satellite Links
summary: Next-generation high-throughput satellites increasingly demodulate and decode on board, so the per-symbol cost of the receiver constrains payload power and throughput. Soft demappers for nonlinear satellite links must therefore produce accurate bit log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) at low cost. We introduce a KAN-LUT demapper, a two-layer Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN) whose learned univariate edge functions are stored as 128-entry lookup tables (LUTs), so that inference needs only table reads, linear interpolation, and additions. We bound the LLR error introduced by the tables and evaluate the demapper on amplitude phase-shift keying (APSK) links with low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding and a nonlinear traveling-wave-tube amplifier. For 16-, 32-, and 64-APSK, KAN-LUT stays within 0.2 dB of a per-cluster Gaussian log-MAP (LogMAP-CG) demapper, while its cost relative to LogMAP-CG falls from 87% to 27% as the order grows. It matches or slightly exceeds multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) at about one fifth of their cost, remains competitive under operating-point mismatch, and needs only tens of kilobytes of tables. KAN-LUT is therefore a low-cost candidate demapper for regenerative payloads.

title: Spatial phase coherence and its applications to masking and adaptive neighborhood sizing in multitemporal InSAR
summary: We examine spatial phase coherence (SPC), a measure of the correlation between the wrapped phase time series of two pixels in a stack of single-look synthetic aperture radar acquisitions. A pixel and its adjacent neighbors share speckle through the point spread function, so that decorrelation alone does not lower their SPC below a floor. We find that masking pixels whose mean SPC to their eight neighbors is well below that floor, as in parts of layover and shadow areas, is an inexpensive complement to geometry-derived layover and shadow masks. For distributed scatterer pixels, averaging SPC over a fixed set of neighbors that share no speckle yields a proxy for the local coherence, the phase coherence indicator (PCI), that is available before the selection of statistically homogeneous pixels (SHPs). In phase estimation, averaging more pixels reduces noise but may also increase the bias in heterogeneous areas. To relax this trade-off, we propose to enhance SHP selection algorithms by scaling the search window size according to the PCI and truncating the set of selected pixels where a smaller nested set agrees clearly better with the phases at the center. In simulations of a TerraSAR-X and a Sentinel-1 stack with 44 and 79 acquisitions, we apply this adaptive neighborhood sizing (ANS) to established amplitude- and covariance-based SHP selection algorithms with thresholds that adapt to the PCI. Without ANS, the largest tested search window size has 13 to 29 % more phase linking error than the best of the tested sizes. With ANS, the largest window has the lowest error of the tested sizes, 11 % lower than that of the same selection at its best tested size without ANS. On a real TerraSAR-X stack, the mask based on SPC flags pixels in building shadows that a terrain model misses. On real Sentinel-1 stacks, ANS preserves dense fringes on a slowly deforming slope and in part on a fast landslide.

title: Cross-Subject Priors for Maximum a Posteriori Estimation of Latent Structure Influence Models in Motor-Imagery EEG With Few Trials
summary: Coupled hidden Markov models such as the latent structure influence model (LSIM) describe how the sensorimotor rhythms of the two hemispheres evolve and interact during motor imagery, but subject-specific maximum likelihood (ML) estimates are unstable when few trials are available. This paper derives a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator for the LSIM whose conjugate prior equals the expected statistics of $\lambda$ pseudo-trials from a population model fitted to other subjects. The M-step remains in closed form, expectation maximization keeps its monotone ascent, and ML ($\lambda=0$) and the population model ($\lambda\to\infty$) are limiting cases. The prior strength was selected on 35 subjects of the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Dataset and applied unchanged to 70 held-out subjects and to BCI Competition IV-2a. With $\lambda=1$ the held-out log-likelihood exceeded that of ML in 61 of 70 subjects (Holm-adjusted $p=9.1\times10^{-8}$) and in all 70 subjects with five training trials per class. A prior learned only from the PhysioNet data improved the held-out likelihood of all nine BCI IV-2a subjects at five trials per class and reduced the error of the joint transition matrix by 61%. Decoding accuracy did not improve ($p=0.17$). Cross-subject priors therefore stabilize few-trial dynamic models of motor-imagery EEG, but they do not improve decoding, which in these data relies mainly on structure shared across subjects.

title: Achievable Information Rate for FTN under a Reduced Complexity BCJR Receiver
summary: The capacity of faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling in additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels has been established and is achieved by Gaussian inputs. However, the capacity of FTN signaling with finite-constellations is not yet fully characterized. The achievable information rate (AIR) provides a lower bound on this constrained capacity by quantifying the rate supported by a specified input distribution and receiver. This paper investigates the AIR of FTN signaling with finite constellations using full-state and reduced-state Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv (BCJR) receivers, with bidirectional decision feedback incorporated into the reduced-state receiver. Especially, the detection problem is formulated in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), where a geometric foundation is established to understand FTN under severe time packing. The formulation establishes that the Ungerboeck metric remains valid even when the noise covariance is singular. We further characterize detection errors geometrically using RKHS distances between competing sequences. We also study outage probability for reduced-state detection, which occurs when AIR is zero, in addition to deriving the zero-AIR outage criterion for reduced-state detection. Unlike ISI-free Nyquist signaling, reduced-state FTN detection can retain residual ISI that causes the receiver to assign excessive confidence to incorrect symbols, leading to outage even at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Our results confirm both the spectral efficiency gains and the feasibility of FTN systems employing finite constellations and realistic receiver architectures.

title: ANNA: Attention-Free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation for Channel Estimation on Regenerative NTN Payloads
summary: Accurate deep learning (DL)-based channel estimation (CE) for non-terrestrial network (NTN) uplinks must meet the processing, power, and latency constraints of regenerative payloads. We propose Attention-free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation (ANNA), a lightweight architecture combining per-resource block (RB) pilot projection, convolutional neighborhood aggregation, and shared reconstruction, with dense-grid expansion only at the output. Evaluation against learned and classical estimators uses paired waveform-generated datasets with receiver frequency correction enabled and disabled. With correction enabled, 16-bit floating point (FP16) deployment on a 10 W Jetson Orin NX achieves 0.372 ms 99th-percentile (P99) latency and 2.15 dB lower mean normalized mean-squared error (NMSE) than the fastest learned baseline at 29.6% higher latency. Relative to the most accurate learned baseline, ANNA is 4.08 times as fast and consumes 80.5% less module energy per sample, with a 1.14 dB accuracy penalty. It meets the adopted 0.5 ms P99 target in all 100 benchmark runs, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-latency-energy trade-off for embedded uplink CE.

title: Functional Information, Optimal Channel Simulation and Lossy Source Coding
summary: We characterize, within a constant number of bits, the minimum achievable rate for several one-shot coding problems, such as channel simulation and lossy source coding. The basis of our work is a new information measure between random variables $X, Y$ that we call the functional information $I_F(X \to Y)$. We show that this quantity characterizes the minimum one-shot rate $R^*(X \to Y)$ of channel simulation, in which a sample $Y \sim P_{Y \mid X}$ is communicated in the presence of common randomness: $I_F(X \to Y) \leq R^*(X \to Y) < I_F(X \to Y) + 1.45$. For the achievability result, we construct an explicit code using the Poisson functional representation. Using these results, we develop new bounds for one-shot variable-rate lossy source coding: given some distortion measure $\Delta$, we use $I_F(X \to Y)$ to define the functional rate-distortion function $R_F$. Then, letting $R_O$ denote the one-shot operational rate-distortion function with private encoder randomness and distortion measure $\Delta$, we make use of our channel simulation result to show that $R_F(D) \leq R_O(D) < R_F(D) + 2.45$ at every positive distortion level $D$. Finally, we generalize our channel simulation result by introducing the Rényi $\alpha$-functional information $I_{F, \alpha}(X \to Y)$ and show that it characterizes the minimum Arimoto-Rényi conditional entropy for channel simulation, ${R^*_\alpha(X \to Y)}$, associated with the Campbell cost: ${I_{F, \alpha}(X \to Y) \leq R^*_{\alpha}(X \to Y) \leq I_{F, \alpha}(X \to Y) + O(1/\alpha)}$.

title: Multi-Library Feature Engineering and Statistically Validated Classification for Power Swing Detection and Stability Assessment
summary: Faults occurring during power swings, and the evolution of a swing into an unstable condition, cause distance-relay maloperation and cascaded outages. This paper identifies faults, faults during power swings, and power swings, and distinguishes stable from unstable swings in a 9-bus WSCC system modeled in PSCAD/EMTDC. Three time-series feature libraries (tsfresh, TSFEL, and tsfeatures) are applied to the 3-phase relay voltages and currents, giving 3286 statistical, temporal, spectral, and fractal descriptors per event window. A two-step feature selection (Boruta all-relevant filtering followed by RFECV- and SHAP-guided minimal-optimal pruning) reduces the feature set to 18 compact, non-redundant features. 14 classifiers spanning linear, kernel/instance-based, probabilistic, neural, and tree-ensemble/boosting families are then benchmarked under repeated stratified cross-validation, with model differences assessed by a Friedman/Nemenyi omnibus-and-post-hoc test and a Nadeau--Bengio corrected paired t-test. Rotation Forest (ROF) identifies the three event types with 99.98% and SVM-RBF distinguishes stable from unstable swings with 97.97% balanced accuracy. The results show that automated, library-driven feature extraction combined with rigorous statistical model comparison achieves near-perfect discrimination while retaining feature-level interpretability through SHAP importance.

title: Joint Antenna Positioning and Dynamic Beam Tracking for MA-Enabled Full-Duplex Secure ISAC Systems: A Flow Matching DRL Approach
summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) improves spectral efficiency but faces significant security challenges in dynamic wireless environments, where the potential eavesdropper is treated as the sensing target. This paper proposes a movable antenna (MA)-enabled full-duplex secure ISAC system that tracks the mobile eavesdropper while safeguarding both uplink and downlink transmissions. Specifically, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) is employed to recursively estimate and predict the eavesdropper's state from radar echoes. Building on the estimated target state, we formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the sum of the uplink and downlink secrecy rates by jointly optimizing the transmit and receive MA positions, uplink and downlink beamforming, artificial noise, and uplink transmit power. The resulting problem is challenging due to its inherent nonconvexity, strong coupling among optimization variables, and time-varying nature. Conventional iterative optimization methods may incur prohibitive computational overhead in dynamic environments, whereas existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods based on unimodal Gaussian or deterministic policies may struggle to capture complex multimodal high-reward action distributions. To address these challenges, we develop a flow matching-based deep reinforcement learning (FMDRL) algorithm for sequential joint decision-making. The proposed algorithm integrates a conditional velocity-field actor with twin critics, generating continuous actions through finite-step Euler integration and employing a deterministic decoder to enforce physical constraints on antenna positions, transmit power, and positive semidefiniteness. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed FMDRL algorithm achieves superior performance in terms of both communication security and target tracking capabilities.

title: Wideband Terahertz Pinching-Antenna Systems (PASS): Bandwidth Limits, Ergodic Rate, and Placement Optimization
summary: Terahertz (THz) bands offer the vast bandwidth that sixth-generation (6G) networks demand, but their severe path loss makes bringing the radiator close to the user decisive. Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) do exactly this, turning path loss into a programmable parameter by sliding radiating points along a dielectric waveguide, which makes THz their native regime. That regime, however, is inherently wideband and the waveguide is dispersive, whereas every existing PASS analysis is single-frequency and assumes a non-dispersive guide. This paper develops the first wideband, dispersion-aware theory of PASS and uncovers a limitation intrinsic to the pinching mechanism. Because co-phasing by physical position equalizes path length only modulo a wavelength, a pinching array is inherently beam-squint limited, and we show its frequency response is a Dirichlet kernel with a closed-form coherence bandwidth and an irreducible dispersion floor that even true-time-delay (TTD) correction cannot remove. A single unifying law governs the behavior, in which array gain trades against both coherence bandwidth and spatial robustness through one invariant that TTD correction breaks, reaching the floor with far fewer delay elements than a conventional array. We further characterize the wideband ergodic rate under random user locations, show that molecular absorption acts as a deterministic taper that multiplies the squint, and derive a simple rule for the rate-optimal number of pinches. Finally, by exploiting the integer structure of co-phasing, we recast the non-convex placement problem as a mixed-integer program that can be solved exactly in polynomial time. Together, these results move PASS from the narrowband, dispersion-blind setting to the wideband, dispersive regime that THz operation actually requires.

title: Target Detection with Tightly-coupled Wideband Antenna Arrays
summary: This paper focuses on tightly coupled antenna (TCA) array systems with high mutual coupling, resulting in wideband signals. We analyze the target detection capability of such systems with joint time and frequency approaches. We assume a target whose echo signals are unknown wideband signals and show the opportunity that TCAs create in target detection. We consider temporal and spectral dynamics of the signal as either constant, slowly or rapidly varying in frequency and time, giving nine possible cases in total. For each case we derive a detector and present thorough analysis for the distribution of the detector test statistic, considering frequency-dependent noise correlation due to mutual coupling. For the cases with a signal changing slowly in at least one domain we propose a novel detection approach based on estimation of the signal via local averaging of the samples. We also derive a detector that results in an upper bound on detection performance for comparison. We compare our analytical results with simulations, showing perfect accuracy of our derived distributions. In addition, we assess the performance of the detectors under various time/frequency variation rates. We show the superior performance of our proposed detection approach in comparison to other detectors including an extended energy detector we derive for correlated noise as well as both frequency and time samples.

title: Weighted Sum-Rate Optimization of Near-Field STAR-RIS-Aided ISAC Systems Under Hardware Impairments
summary: This paper investigates weighted sum-rate (WSR) optimization for a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS)-assisted multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system operating under the energy splitting (ES) protocol. A hybrid propagation model is considered, where the base station (BS)-STAR-RIS channel follows far-field propagation, whereas the STAR-RIS-user channels are modeled using near-field spherical wavefronts. Practical hardware impairments (HWIs), including STAR-RIS phase perturbations and signal-dependent additive distortion at the BS and user equipment (UEs), are incorporated into the system model. Under this framework, the WSR maximization problem is formulated subject to radar beampattern, quality-of-service, transmit-power, and STAR-RIS ES constraints. The resulting problem is highly non-convex due to the coupling among the active beamformers, passive STAR-RIS coefficients, and HWI-dependent signal-to interference-plus-noise ratio expressions. An alternating optimization (AO)-based successive convex approximation framework is developed to iteratively solve the active and passive beamforming subproblems. Numerical results demonstrate stable convergence of the proposed algorithm and consistent WSR improvement over direct-link transmission. Besides, severe HWIs also lead to WSR saturation in the high transmit-power regime, whereas stringent sensing constraints reduce communication throughput. Increasing the STAR-RIS aperture and the number of BS antennas improves the achievable WSR, although the performance gain becomes limited under strong hardware distortion.

title: Miniaturized Low-Cost 3-D Printed High-Permittivity Dielectric Transmissive LP-to-CP Converter for L-Band Satellite Communications
summary: A low-cost, miniaturized, additively manufactured transmissive linear-to-circular polarization converter for L-band air and space communication systems is presented. The proposed polarizer employs an in-house-fabricated high-permittivity dielectric medium, realized using a 3-D printed polylactic acid (PLA) enclosure filled with a TiO$_2$--water mixture. Variation in the effective permittivity is achieved by adjusting the mixture filling fraction. The selected 60\% filling fraction corresponds to an effective relative permittivity of 11.3 at 1 GHz. The high-permittivity loading enables miniaturization of the polarizer height and area by reducing the anisotropic dielectric unit-cell dimensions to $\boldsymbol{0.037\lambda_0 \times 0.037\lambda_0 \times 0.22\lambda_0}$. An additively manufactured polarizer with overall dimensions $\boldsymbol{0.83\lambda_0 \times 0.77\lambda_0 \times 0.22\lambda_0}$ is experimentally validated using a compact linearly polarized feed source. The measured results demonstrate LP-to-CP conversion, with a 3 dB axial ratio of 12\% and insertion loss of less than 0.6 dB. Radiation-pattern measurements at 1 GHz show LHCP-to-RHCP discrimination levels of 19 and 24 dB in the \textbf{\textit{xz}}- and \textbf{\textit{yz}}-planes, respectively. The proposed configuration combines miniaturization, LP-to-CP conversion, and low-cost additive manufacturing, making it promising for UAV-mounted and other size-constrained L-band satellite communication terminals.

title: SiGMA: Site-Grounded Multi-Modal ISAC Data Generation for Environment-Aware Communications
summary: Learning-based multi-modal integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) requires data that associate environmental observations with the wireless response generated by the same site and dynamic scene state. Acquiring such data at new sites requires sensor calibration, coordinated measurements, and cross-modal association. We present site-grounded multi-modal ISAC data generation (SiGMA), which combines OpenStreetMap (OSM), Overture Maps, and procedural three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction to create georeferenced urban scenes. A shared scene geometry and time-indexed actor state link synchronized red-green-blue (RGB) images, light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds, positioning records, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) Radar in-phase and quadrature (IQ) samples, and ray-traced wireless channels. For configurable reflected propagation under direct-link blockage, SiGMA generates optional reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) component channels for phase-configuration evaluation across shared scene states. The evaluation results demonstrate that the framework improves zero-shot beam prediction performance on real DeepSense 6G measurements compared with an OSM-derived synthetic-data baseline. A camera-assisted RIS case study further demonstrates the generation of sensing-associated supervision for configurable reflected propagation. The dataset generation pipeline is available at this https URL.

title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ over the Unit Quaternions
summary: We extend the recursive construction of perfect and odd perfect sequences over the simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ of Blake to arrays of any dimension. The three operations of that construction act on one direction of an array at a time, and are valid whenever the array is periodic in the remaining directions. Starting from a perfect array $P$ of shape $M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ they give perfect arrays of shape $2^a\times M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ for every $a\ge0$, with explicit index functions and with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$ in the lifted direction; from $a=5$ on these arrays are, in general, Kronecker products of a sequence with $P$ in neither order. Applied direction by direction, the construction gives perfect arrays over $\Qe$ in every shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$, and in every shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_{d-1}}\times N$ for which a perfect sequence of length $N$ over $\Qe$ exists. The contrast with the binary alphabet is sharp: a perfect binary array of shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ exists only when $\sum a_k$ is even and $\max a_k\le\frac12\sum a_k+1$, by a theorem of Jedwab and Kraemer on Menon difference sets in abelian $2$-groups, whereas over $\Qe$ there is no constraint on the shape. We also show that, unlike the one-dimensional case, single arrays carrying a non-central twist do exist in two dimensions, and determine where the one-dimensional non-existence argument breaks.

title: Do Hierarchical Networks Actually Learn? Insights from Word-of-Mouth Estimation
summary: We study recursive estimation of a constant state vector by a hierarchical network of asymmetrically informed linear estimators, modeled as a directed tree. Only the leaves observe the regression signal, whereas every other estimator learns by word of mouth from noisy signal estimates relayed by its children. Authority within the hierarchy is expressed through common prior information: after each round, every estimator adopts the estimate and error covariance broadcast by the root. The more accurate this common information, the larger the effective noise variance on local observations, which makes estimation intrinsically self-defeating. The resulting performance is the subject of this paper. We show that recursive least-squares (RLS) estimators do learn the state in mean square, albeit slowly. Under strong persistency of excitation, the broadcast error covariance decays polynomially in time, at a rate that we characterize by upper and lower bounds of matching order. The exponent is determined by the smallest number of relays between a leaf and the root, and it decreases exponentially with this number.

title: Network-Native DNN Architecture Synthesis for Distributed Inference
summary: Distributed deep neural network (DNN) inference typically follows a model-first paradigm, in which a predefined DNN is partitioned and deployed over a physical network. On irregular communication-computation topologies, however, this approach can create transmission bottlenecks and leave distributed resources underutilized. This paper reverses this perspective and asks: given a physical network, what kind of DNN can it naturally support? To answer this question, we propose a network-native DNN architecture synthesis paradigm in which the physical network topology directly defines inter-node neural dependencies. Neural computation is allocated across nodes under communication, computation, storage, synchronization, and latency constraints. We establish structural properties of the synthesis problem and develop linear programming (LP)-based Architecture Synthesis (LPAS), an efficient topology-guided algorithm that produces a feasible architecture with a computable bound on suboptimality. Experiments on physical networks of different sizes show that LPAS achieves relative gaps below 0.6% to the LP-derived upper bound, with substantially lower runtime than direct mixed-integer LP optimization on larger networks. Under matched network deadlines, the network-native architectures activate more compute nodes and utilize a larger proportion of available model-storage capacity than the model-first baseline. After training, the network-native models achieve higher classification accuracy across all evaluated dataset-precision settings, with the average gain of up to 10.69%. This network-native design paradigm thus turns the physical network from a deployment constraint into an architecture design primitive.

title: Practical Semantic Communication for General-Purpose Networks: Compression of High-Dimensional Embeddings Under Quantization
summary: This paper introduces a practical framework for semantic communication over wireless channels, focusing on the compression of high-dimensional embeddings under quantization and channel errors. Building upon a relaxed Gaussian Information Bottleneck (GIB) model, the approach provides analytical solutions for task-relevant information preservation, even with non-Gaussian targets. The framework relaxes traditional Gaussian assumptions, enabling effective compression for discrete and complex data such as text embeddings. It derives closed-form gradients for optimizing the compression matrix and establishes bounds linking continuous representations to discrete, noisy system performance. Comprehensive experiments on text classification tasks demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms task-agnostic quantization-based compression methods, maintaining high semantic fidelity at low bit budgets per embedding. The approach offers a scalable, interpretable, and resource-efficient solution for deploying semantic communication in general-purpose networks.

title: Analysis and Design of Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes for Pulsed-Jamming-Resilient Space Telemetry
summary: Jamming is a major threat to space telemetry downlinks, which operate under severe power and bandwidth constraints. This paper develops a jamming-aware analysis and design framework for protograph-based spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) codes. For pulsed jamming with jamming state information (JSI) at the receiver, we derive a two-state protograph-based extrinsic information transfer (PEXIT) recursion that tracks the messages originating from clean and jammed symbols separately and merges them at the check nodes through a mutual-information-matched Gaussian approximation. For non-interleaved pulsed jamming, we map each pulse realization, through the serialization of the lifted codeword, to a profile of jammed fractions over the variable-node types, and we prove that, under random lifting, this profile determines the local channel-state statistics. The resulting position-dependent thresholds are the objective of a constrained differential-evolution search over protographs, coupling memories, and edge spreadings. At different code rates, the designed ensembles are compared with the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) accumulate, repeat-by-4, and jagged accumulate (AR4JA) LDPC codes whose block length matches the SC-LDPC constraint length, with longer AR4JA codes whose block length is comparable with the size of the sliding window decoder, and with non-optimized SC-LDPC codes. Under pulsed jamming with random pulse positions and with JSI, the ensembles designed over random pulse realizations, decoded through sliding window decoding, reach a bit error rate of $10^{-4}$ at lower signal-to-noise ratios than all the benchmarks.

title: Improving Radio SLAM via Information Sharing: Collaborative Performance Bounds
summary: This paper studies the fundamental performance limits of radio-based collaborative simultaneous localization and mapping (C-SLAM) in dense vehicular environments towards the 6G integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) era. We consider a collaborative estimation task consisting of multiple user equipments (UEs) with unknown local state variables together with joint estimation of unknown states of the environment landmarks or targets, using cellular radio measurements. Specifically, a posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) is derived for such centralized multi-UE cellular radio SLAM with information sharing, capturing the effects of the number of involved UEs, their geometric configuration, and their mutually different abilities to measure or observe different landmarks. The analysis reveals how information sharing scales with UE density, identifies regimes of diminishing returns, and provides estimator-independent limits for collaborative radio-based environment mapping and localization. The provided numerical results validate the proposed framework in a vehicular system context, while also demonstrating substantial gains against more ordinary single-UE radio SLAM approach.

title: The Exact Optimal Delivery Scheme for the Cyclically $L$-Separated Placement in Multi-Access Coded Caching
summary: This paper investigates the $(K, L, M, N)$ multi-access coded caching (MACC) system introduced by Hachem et al. The system consists of a server storing $N$ equal-sized files, $K$ cache nodes, each with a storage capacity of $M$ files, and $K$ users, each accessing $L$ consecutive cache nodes in a cyclic wrap-around topology. The server transmits coded information to the users via an error-free capacitated broadcast channel, such that each user obtains its own requested file as a combination of the server transmission and the accessible caches' content. Our objective is to minimize the worst-case transmission load over all possible user demands. First, for the cyclically $L$-separated placement, we derive a new converse bound using the acyclic index coding bound. By carefully counting all valid cache supports, the proposed converse improves upon an existing bound for the same placement. We then develop a linear coded caching scheme based on a novel determinant-based interference alignment strategy, which achieves the new converse bound exactly. Exploiting the determinant structure of a random generating matrix (each of whose columns corresponds to one user), this scheme simultaneously aligns interference across all users into low-dimensional subspaces, while preserving the decodability of their desired packets. Furthermore, by averaging acyclic index coding bounds over cyclic user permutations, we derive a general converse bound applicable to arbitrary uncoded cache placements. By combining the proposed scheme with memory sharing, we demonstrate that the achievable transmission load is within a factor of two of the global bound under uncoded placement. Finally, theoretical and numerical comparisons demonstrate that the proposed scheme generally achieves a strictly lower load than existing schemes.

title: Risk-Aware Handover Management Approach for Non-Terrestrial Networks with the NTN-Connect Simulator
summary: The continuous movement of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites in non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) leads to frequent handovers, requiring joint optimization of visibility duration, transmit power, and user quality-of-service (QoS). This work address this issue by proposing a risk-aware handover management framework that minimizes transmit power and maximizes admitted users under per-satellite power budgets and user-rate chance constraints, while a preference score term penalizes short duration associations. We decompose the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) into an inner power allocation subproblem and an outer generalized assignment association subproblem. The inner subproblem reformulates the chance constraint into its deterministic counterpart using the value-at-risk (VaR) closed-form. The obtained transmit power allocation is then used in the association subproblem, which is solved optimally using an off-the-shelf solver. Finally, we employ the polynomial-complexity Hungarian algorithm to solve the relaxed assignment problem and enforce the per-satellite power budget using a knapsack algorithm. Simulations, using the proposed NTN-Connect simulator, on the OneWeb and Starlink constellations show that the proposed low-complexity solution achieves near-optimal performance and better performance compared to the risk-aware maximum stay (RA-MST) and risk-aware maximum received signal received power (RA-MRSRP) baselines. On the Starlink constellation, it increases the inter-handover interval (IHI) from $0.37$ to $1.47$~min, reducing the handover rate by $75\%$. At a maximum-IHI operating point, it reduces the total transmit power by 1.1 dBW (22\%) while increasing the admission rate from 97.4\% to 99.3\%.

title: Observing Earth's ionospheric irregularities from the Moon
summary: Radio signals that propagate through the Earth's ionosphere carry information about possible irregular plasma structures. Such irregularities manifest themselves as amplitude signatures that depend on the propagation and observation geometry [1, 2]. Conventional ground and low-Earth-orbit (LEO) measurements sample these effects close to Earth. Here we present a systematic characterization of terrestrial ionospheric irregularities using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) amplitude observations from the lunar surface, at distances of approximately 356,000-398,000 km from Earth's surface [3]. Using nearly 93 h of 1-Hz lunar-surface observations of GPS L1/L5 and Galileo E1/E5a collected by the Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE), we reconstruct the propagation and scanning geometry to characterize the spatiotemporal signatures of amplitude and phase fluctuations. At lunar distance, the Fresnel scale approaches its finite-source limit, extending the observations to a propagation regime beyond conventional near-Earth configurations. Detrended receiver-reported carrier-to-noise density ratios (${\delta}C/N_0$) reveal pronounced polar amplitude fluctuations at both frequency bands, also visible in the original measurements. Within the regions and local times sampled, large fluctuations occur in about 30% of valid one-minute polar windows, compared with less than 5% in either the equatorial or mid-latitude band. These findings support using the lunar surface as a vantage point for studying Earth's polar ionospheric irregularities and testing how propagation and scanning relative to the magnetic field shape their amplitude signatures. Future lunar observations could extend this approach to long-term monitoring of Earth's ionospheric irregularities

title: A High-Resolution TOA Estimation Algorithm Based on Compressed Sensing for Coherent Multi-Band Signals
summary: High-resolution time-of-arrival (ToA) estimation is crucial for accurate ranging and localization in future wireless networks. While multi-band operation can synthesize a large virtual bandwidth by probing several separated subbands, the resulting non-contiguous frequency layout induces pronounced sidelobes and dense local maxima in the delay response, making reliable ToA estimation challenging. This paper studies coherent multi-band ToA estimation from a single multi-band channel state information (CSI) snapshot. We derive a multiband least-squares formulation and analyze its point-spread function (PSF) and Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) to characterize the effects of the subband layout on delay accuracy and sidelobe ambiguity. Building on this analysis, we propose a low complexity two-stage particle swarm optimization estimator and incorporate it into orthogonal matching pursuit with a RELAX-type cyclic refinement procedure for multipath delay estimation, mitigating basis mismatch and improving robustness to the dense local maxima induced by non-contiguous multi-band layouts. Numerical results are consistent with the PSF and CRB analyses and show that the proposed framework approaches the CRB in the single-path setting and achieves accurate multipath delay estimation with low computational complexity. Real channel measurements further validate the predicted impact of different subband layouts on delay-estimation performance.
